definitions.explanation: Having more than enough money and material possessions to live comfortably. A neutral, non-flashy way to describe someone who is financially comfortable.

examples.japanese: {裕福|ゆうふく}な{家庭|かてい}に{育|そだ}った。
examples.english: She grew up in a wealthy family.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{裕福|ゆうふく}ではないが、{幸|しあわ}せな{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}っている。
examples.english: He isn't wealthy, but he leads a happy life.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{比較的|ひかくてき}{裕福|ゆうふく}な{世帯|せたい}が{多|おお}く、{教育|きょういく}{水準|すいじゅん}も{高|たか}い。
examples.english: This area has many relatively affluent households, and the standard of education is also high.

notes:
USAGE:
A neutral, respectful way to describe wealth. Less flashy than {金持|かねも}ち (rich person) and more dignified than {リッチ} (rich). Often used to describe families and backgrounds rather than individuals.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {裕福|ゆうふく}: wealthy, well-off (dignified, moderate tone)
- {金持|かねも}ち: rich person (direct, casual)
- {富裕|ふゆう}: affluent (formal, often in statistics)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {裕福|ゆうふく}な{家庭|かてい}: wealthy family
- {裕福|ゆうふく}な{暮|く}らし: affluent lifestyle
